source.title: A PDE-based Explanation of Extreme Numerical Sensitivities and Edge of Stability in Training Neural Networks
source.authors: Yuxin Sun; Dong-Sheng Lao; A. Yezzi; G. Sundaramoorthi

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests an edge-of-stability explanation using a PDE model and simplified networks, rather than the wide-network training setup in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper's CIFAR-10 ResNet and other Section 4 experiments measure test-accuracy variability and weight divergence from floating-point perturbations, not the training-error or stability behaviors named by the claim versions. The PDE examples and simplified CNN experiments report loss and sharpness behavior relevant to V5.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures loss and Hessian sharpness during gradient descent and tests an explanation of V5's edge-of-stability component using simplified CNNs and full-batch network experiments. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate but incomplete. The authors report that floating-point errors can amplify into test-accuracy variation comparable to batch-selection variation. Their simplified CNN analysis explains how nonlinear dynamics can restrain numerical instabilities, connects these instabilities to edge-of-stability behavior, and predicts dependence on network structure, learning rate and weight decay.
record.recipe_differences: Uses PDE stability analysis and simplified CNN experiments, including a one-datum example; does not apply the squared-loss wide-network recipe described in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes whether runs are stable or exhibit restrained instabilities. Network depth changes the observed stability boundary in the reported experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Last-bit floating-point perturbations produce test-accuracy variation comparable to stochastic batch selection and cause optimization paths to separate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Floating-point errors can amplify during standard neural-network training and materially affect final test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: The Beltrami PDE remains bounded at 10 or 100 times its strict stable step size and diverges at 1000 times that size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nonlinear PDE optimization can exhibit restrained numerical instability above its strict stability limit.

record.problems: The relevant edge-of-stability results are simplified PDE/CNN experiments, including a one-training-datum case. Figure 6 values are not numerically stated in the text, and the reported loss behavior does not establish low training loss after the sharpness crosses the boundary.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. Figures 7–9 report depth and regularization comparisons, but do not measure the sharpness-threshold behavior named by V5.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the benefit of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in deep plain batch-normalized CNNs and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for learning speed and trainable depth.

The wide-network squared-loss catapult trajectory relative to the initial linearized-model threshold; recovery to low loss; long-term loss reduction while sharpness hovers at the threshold; and eventual divergence despite starting below that threshold.
Matched comparisons of training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization or Fixup.

missing.what: The one-layer CNN's loss blows up for learning rates above 0.1, whereas rates between 0.03 and 0.1 produce restrained oscillations. These outcomes supply the missing larger-rate divergence comparison, although they use regularized cross-entropy rather than V5's squared-loss recipe.

Full-batch training at learning rate 2/150 is reported stable for the two-layer tanh network, while doubling its depth produces loss spikes and sharpness above the stability bound. Although rows_left_out names Figure 8, its assertion that this figure does not measure sharpness-threshold behavior is incorrect.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's limits_scope verdict: stable low-rate controls are compatible with V5, and failure to establish low-loss recovery is an untested component rather than a demonstrated limitation. Figures 7 and 9 compare stability across depths, not the training-error degradation or shortcut benefit specified by V3.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test wide networks trained with squared loss, learning rates above the initial linearized-model stability limit, or full-batch training in which sharpness hovers at the threshold while loss continues falling over longer times. It does not test the divergence cases described in the version.

rows.subject: one-layer CNN in Section 5.4
rows.operation_detail: Discretized nonlinear gradient-descent PDE; plotted loss versus iterations.
rows.value: Figure only; text states the learning rates are stable.
rows.note: Text states normalized sharpness stays below 2 for these stable learning rates; it does not state a final loss value.
rows.check: A stable-loss control does not establish recovery after crossing a stability threshold. No final loss value can be read from the supplied text. The objective includes weight decay, with alpha=20.

rows.subject: one-layer CNN in Section 5.4
rows.operation_detail: Discretized nonlinear gradient-descent PDE; plotted normalized sharpness over iterations.
rows.measure: Normalized sharpness (learning rate times maximum Hessian eigenvalue)
rows.value: Figure only; text states normalized sharpness is always below 2.
rows.check: Normalized sharpness stays below 2, so edge-of-stability behavior is absent in this low-rate control. This is not contrary evidence because V5 does not predict threshold crossing at every learning rate.

rows.subject: one-layer CNN in Section 5.4
rows.operation_detail: Discretized nonlinear gradient-descent PDE; plotted loss versus iterations.
rows.value: Figure only; text describes restrained instabilities (oscillations).
rows.note: The text does not state that loss reaches a low value after the oscillations.
rows.check: Restrained loss oscillations establish bounded instability, but the supplied text does not establish subsequent low loss or continued long-term loss reduction. The objective includes weight decay, with alpha=20.

rows.subject: one-layer CNN in Section 5.4
rows.operation_detail: Discretized nonlinear gradient-descent PDE; plotted normalized sharpness over iterations.
rows.measure: Normalized sharpness (learning rate times maximum Hessian eigenvalue)
rows.value: Figure only; text states normalized sharpness oscillates and can exceed 2.
rows.note: Directly bears on exceeding the classical stability boundary; the text does not say sharpness remains above 2 throughout.
rows.check: Correct for the threshold-crossing component: normalized sharpness oscillates and can exceed 2. This row alone does not establish progressive sharpening, persistent hovering near 2, or falling loss.

relationships.condition: One-layer Swish CNN, one training image, regularized cross-entropy, learning rates 0.05, 0.07 and 0.09
relationships.reason: R3 and R4 show restrained loss oscillations while normalized sharpness oscillates and exceeds 2, supporting the edge-of-stability component in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: Loss oscillations remained restrained while normalized sharpness oscillated and exceeded 2.

relationships.condition: Four-layer tanh fully connected network on CIFAR-5k, full-batch cross-entropy training without weight decay, learning rate 2/150
relationships.reason: Section 6.2 explicitly reports loss spikes and sharpness exceeding the stability bound in Figure 8; this verdict rests on text omitted from the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Training exhibited loss spikes and sharpness exceeding the stability bound.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
